item.title: 'We did likewise': Mohit Ulva reveals why India celebrated aggressively after beating Pakistan
item.description: India U-19 batter Mohit Ulva has explained the emotions behind the team's animated celebrations following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final, insisting that the players were simply celebrating their triumph and had no intention of provoking their opponents. Mohit, who played a decisive role in India's remarkable chase with an unbeaten 49 off just 26 balls, said the celebrations were a natural reaction to the occasion, given the intensity of an India-Pakistan contest and the fact that it was a final. The celebrations that followed, however, became a talking point, with several Indian players facing criticism on social media for their aggressive gestures towards the Pakistani players. Mohit revealed that the celebrations were a spontaneous expression of the emotions surrounding an India-Pakistan final. He also recalled how the Indian youngsters had not taken Pakistan's celebrations during the league-stage encounter personally. "It is natural. It was an India vs Pakistan match, and additionally, a final. The way they celebrated after beating us in the league stage. Actually, we were not even taking their celebration personally. We were thinking that they were celebrating their own victory. It doesn't matter what they do. "We did likewise. We were celebrating our own victory. It had emotions, aggression, and everything. We weren't doing it to show them anything. We were celebrating among ourselves, and everything was natural," Mohit told Star Sports. 'I couldn't believe I had finished it' India were staring at defeat after slipping to 252/8 in the 42nd over of the chase. However, Mohit and Manal Chauhan refused to give up, putting together a crucial 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket to keep India's hopes alive. Manal scored 47 off 32 balls before departing, leaving India needing 36 more runs with just one wicket remaining. Mohit then received support from No. 11 C Venkata, who remained unbeaten on 11 off eight deliveries. The equation eventually came down to three runs off the final ball, with Mohit finding the boundary to seal the title. Recalling the extraordinary finish, the youngster admitted that he was initially unable to process what had happened. "Actually, I was completely zoned out after hitting three runs on one ball with a four. I didn't know that everyone was running to me; everything was happening. "It was done; I finished the game. Until it was over, I believed that I would finish it. But after I did it, I couldn't believe that I had finished it. So, I was a little zoned out. "After a while, I realised that it was actually over. Everyone was getting up, everyone was celebrating. So, I celebrated a little. I went to the supporters of India, who were sitting there the whole day. I went to them and celebrated with them. It's a very good feeling. Even now, it's a very good feeling for me. Because for my family, for my country, for India, it's a good feeling to win such a match," he added. '

item.title: Ciryl Gane Needs A Homecoming Fight In France After UFC 334
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Ciryl Gane walked out of Madison Square Garden with his UFC heavyweight title intact on Saturday night. He defeated Josh Hokit by unanimous decision, but the reception felt wrong for a fighter who just set a new record for strikes in a single heavyweight bout. Gane landed 298 total strikes and Hokit threw 243, for a combined 541 strikes, which ESPN reported as a division record. The Frenchman displayed skill, but fans in the arena treated him like a villain rather than a champion. UFC CEO Dana White admitted he once thought Hokit was a “bigmouthed goofball” before the fight took place. White changed his tune after seeing Hokit push the champion backward with relentless pressure throughout the five-round war. “I respect the s— out of that guy,” White said during the postfight news conference, adding that Hokit is the real deal. By enduring Gane’s volume and electrifying the crowd with a massive slam to close the first round, Hokit earned this respect. A Homecoming in France Gane has spent years playing the role of the bad guy, even after beating top contenders like Alex Pereira in June. He lost to Jon Jones in 2023 and faced controversy with Francis Ngannou in 2022, but his résumé proves he belongs at the top. The UFC should stop booking him in hostile markets and finally give him a fight in his home country of France. As one of the top pound-for-pound fighters globally, Gane has constructed an impressive record and merits a cheering crowd. The Tactical Mistake in the Co-Main While Gane won the main event, Amanda Nunes made a costly tactical error in the co-main event against Kayla Harrison. The former two-time champion returned from retirement but was outplayed by the reigning bantamweight champion, who imposed her own game. Despite possessing the striking ability and experience to win, Nunes could not dictate the pace or terms of the engagement. Hokit said in his postfight interview that he will “rejoice in my suffering.” He promised that even if people kick him when he is down, he will still break their leg one day. Gane credited Hokit’s approach after the bout, noting that the world took him lightly but not the champion himself. “This guy is a motherf—er,” Gane said about his challenger. Gane landed 237 significant strikes, shattering the UFC heavyweight record for a single fight.

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur Urged To Move In For This Arsenal Forward: Should De Zerbi Go For Him?
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur Urged To Move In For This Arsenal Forward: Should De Zerbi Go For Him? In a recent interview with The Last Word On Spurs , David Pleat urged his former club Tottenham Hotspur to move in for Arsenal forward Viktor Gyokeres. Pleat said, “There aren’t many out there; there’s a very small amount of strikers. “Are you going to buy Lankshear back now for £50 million? He’s the top scorer in the Championship, our boy. “So where are you going to get? Are Arsenal going to give us someone like Jesus, or someone they don’t want? He’s gone already, but Gyokeres, perhaps. Who else is there? “[Brian] Brobbey gave us trouble… [Dominic] Calvert-Lewin is very good in the air but had injury problems. When you are signing a striker, it’s about what type of striker. Is he exceptionally good in the air, is he a bully-type striker like Delap or is a clever front player, more like Havertz?” Gyokeres’ Growing Struggles In North London Gyokeres has struggled to earn regular first-team starts for Arsenal in this campaign so far as he has fallen behind Kai Havertz in Mikel Arteta’s pecking order. The 28-year-old registered two goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Gunners this season in all competitions. The Swedish talent is currently among the most talented forwards in the Premier League. Hence, Tottenham would do well to bring him on board next year. LONDON, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 07: Viktor Gyokeres of Arsenal runs with the ball during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Arsenal FC and Hull City at Emirates Stadium on November 07, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) His current contract at the Emirates Stadium will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it difficult for Spurs to land him on the cheap this January or at the end of this campaign. Should Tottenham Hotspur Boss Roberto De Zerbi Go For Gyokeres? Gyokeres is proficient at finding a yard of space for himself to get some strikes in at goal. He has the vision to engineer the odd chance for his teammates to score and is a decent dribbler with the ball at his feet. Standing at 1.89m, the Swedish forward is a strong presence in the air as well. However, there are some question marks on whether he can find a consistent run of form in the Premier League if Spurs manage to snap him up next year. We can expect Gyokeres to add more quality and depth to Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi’s frontline. He is capable of challenging for a regular first-team spot at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. At 28, Gyokeres is about to enter his prime, which makes him a decent choice for Spurs to pursue in 2027. Hence, Tottenham would be wise to go for a striker with his skill set soon.

item.title: LeBron James Returns For Sixers As Back-To-Back Looms
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is set to return to the Philadelphia 76ers lineup for Sunday’s home game against the Indiana Pacers. The 41-year-old star missed Thursday’s victory over the Toronto Raptors to manage low back and sciatica issues, marking his third absence in the team’s first 13 games. This is a massive boost for a team that has struggled to find consistency without its veteran leader. The Sixers have been careful with James’ workload all season. He has not played on consecutive days yet this year as the team manages his health. Nick Nurse now faces a tough choice on how much to play him before the team travels to Brooklyn for a road game on Monday. James struggled in his last outing against Boston, scoring only 11 points on 4-of-12 shooting in 29 minutes. In his first season with the Sixers, he maintains averages of 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 6.5 assists across 10 appearances. His passing ability remains a key asset even if his scoring has dipped. A Tough Road Ahead The Pacers enter Sunday’s game looking for their third straight win after beating the New York Knicks in NBA Cup play on Friday. While dealing with their own injury concerns, Indiana has relied heavily on Pascal Siakam. The Sixers have managed to keep winning despite the heavy load on James and Joel Embiid. Tyrese Maxey led the team with 27 points in the win over Toronto, while Anfernee Simons added 17 off the bench. Rookie VJ Edgecombe also contributed 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists in that game. Philadelphia has a difficult path in the NBA Cup after a heavy 24-point loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 6. That loss hurt their point differential significantly and put them behind in the group race. The team now needs big wins against tough opponents like the Heat and Pacers to stay in the hunt. Sixers Wire reports that the Sixers, Cavaliers, Heat, Knicks, and Pacers are among the teams battling for a next-round spot. The math for Philadelphia is unforgiving, and every point matters. Back-to-Back Concerns According to The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Chris Hine, Thursday’s absence was James’ first that was not related to a back-to-back schedule. This makes his availability for Monday’s game against the Brooklyn Nets a major question mark. The team must decide if playing Sunday is worth the risk of burning him out for the road trip. James has four full days of rest before Sunday, which gave him extra recovery time. LeBron James has not been officially confirmed as a starter yet, though his absence from the injury report suggests he is expected to play.

item.title: Blues Offense Stalls Again In Ugly Loss To Florida
item.description: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images A 4-1 loss to the Florida Panthers on Saturday night meant the St. Louis Blues could not achieve three straight wins. This loss dropped the team to 9-9-2 on the season, a record that makes it hard to call them a true contender. Jacob Markstrom recorded 21 saves for Florida as Dylan Holloway netted the single goal for St. Louis. Joel Hofer stopped 24 shots, but it was not enough to keep the game close. A Special Night with Ugly Results Saturday was supposed to be about celebrating Keith Tkachuk. Supporters had a chance to celebrate a legend as the Blues recognized his Hockey Hall of Fame induction. His sons, Matthew and Brady, played for the Panthers that night, adding a personal touch to the ceremony. Robert Thomas even wore a Tkachuk jersey to the arena, a nod to the time he lived with the family. The ceremonial faceoff used sticks Keith actually used during his career. It was a great moment for the family and the fans, but the result on the ice was a disaster. The team could not translate that emotional energy into goals. Offense Just Does Not Exist The Blues struggled to generate anything offensively from the start, managing just two shots on goal in the first period. Florida had 10 shots, and they capitalized on a pair of penalties to take an early lead. Brady Tkachuk opened the scoring with a toe drag, beating Hofer glove-side. Dmitry Kulikov made it 2-0 after a deflection off Colton Parayko’s stick. The second period offered no help, as St. Louis failed to register a single shot on its power play. For the seventh time this season, the Blues managed to score one goal or fewer. According to The Hockey News , they have now been outscored 16-6 in the four games where they tried to win three straight. “It’s something we’re trying to work on, right,” Blues forward Jake Neighbours said. “I wish I had the answer for you,” Neighbours added after playing in his 300th NHL game. Defense Breaks Down Fast Defensive mistakes doomed the Blues before the offense could even try to fix them. The Panthers scored early and often, building a lead the Blues could not chip away at. Anton Lundell added a goal in the second period, and Sam Reinhart made it 4-1 in the third with a slick move past Parayko. With one game remaining before the quarter mark, the team currently trails the second wild card spot in the Western Conference by three points. “More intensity and driving the net harder and getting pucks there more often,” Blues coach Jim Montgomery said. The team has two days to regroup before their next game. The Blues will look to finish off this two-game homestand strong when they come back Tuesday against Anaheim.

item.title: SDSU men's basketball goes to 4-0 after beating Northern Colorado
item.description: South Dakota State men's basketball moved to 4-0 on the season after a dominant display in Rapid City on Saturday, Nov. 14, beating Northern Colorado 71-46. The 4-0 start is the Jackrabbits' best since 2015-16, when they started 6-0. South Dakota State plays Mayville State and Idaho State to tie that record, then a home game against Abilene Christian could surpass it. It wasn't an offensive showcase on either side, but South Dakota State's defense held Northern Colorado to 26.5% (13-for-49) from the field. The Bears were just 3-for-22 (13.6%) from three. The Jackrabbit offense wasn't incredible, but Jon Mekonnen, Joe Sayler and EJ Ryans all scored in double figures. The trio scored 14, 13 and 10 points, respectively. Mekonnen added 11 rebounds, while Sayler had six assists. Davis Kern pitched in nine points and Alec Squires had eight points and eight boards. South Dakota State will look to make it 5-0 at home against Mayville State at 7 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 16. item.title: Xavi hopes good memories of Berlin in 2015 help Dutch beat Germany
item.description: Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez attends a press conference, ahead of Monday's UEFA National League soccer match against Germany. (is associated with: «Xavi hopes good memories of Berlin in 2015 help Dutch beat Germany») Christian Charisius/dpa Netherlands coach Xavi is returning to Berlin's Olympic Stadium "with very good memories" ahead of the final Nations League group game against Germany on Monday. The Dutch go into the game as group leaders and virtually certain quarter-finalists. "It is a very good, very difficult test for us. It will be a tough game against a strong opponent, a big challenge," the Spain 2010 World Cup winner told a news conference. In his last game for Barcelona, Xavi celebrated winning the Champions League title in Berlin in 2015. Although he only came on late in the 3-1 win over Juventus, he was able to receive the trophy as captain. "It was my last game. We won the cup. My family and friends were here. It was a big, a great evening," Xavi added. He said that after the recent 7-0 win against Greece, his team were full of self-confidence. After the 1-1 draw in the first group meeting between the Dutch and Germans, Xavi now knows how significant the 50th duel between the neighbouring nations is. "I understand the rivalry better now, I know how important the game is," he said.

item.title: NASCAR Drivers Lose Power Over Crew Chief Changes
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Two of the biggest names in NASCAR admitted they had no voice in recent crew chief changes. Alex Bowman and Shane van Gisbergen confirmed they were not consulted before their teams swapped leaders. The moves happened right after the 2026 season ended, leaving drivers to accept new bosses they did not choose. This shift shows a clear power gap between the people behind the wheel and the teams that hire their staff. Drivers Feel Shut Out Alex Bowman, who is wrapping up his final Cup season in 2027, lost Blake Harris as his crew chief. Harris is moving to Trackhouse Racing to lead Shane van Gisbergen’s team. Bowman told Autoweek he was not part of the decision-making process. When questioned regarding his participation in the crew chief situation, “I haven’t really been a part of that,” Bowman replied, according to Autoweek . He added that other people likely have a better view of the changes. The Arizona native noted that not every race team operates the same way, which makes finding the right fit harder for drivers. Van Gisbergen faces a similar reality with his own crew chief, Stephen Doran, returning to Spire Motorsports. He described the process as simply accepting who you get and making it work. “You kind of just get put with who you are and work it out from there,” Van Gisbergen said. He believes the final call rests entirely with the team owners and managers. Why Leadership Matters More Because of this, he needs a crew chief who can step up and make tough calls. “I’m not the most natural leader in the world,” Bowman said. He explained that having a strong leader in the booth is vital for his success. “I’m shy and awkward and kind of stick to myself. So having a good, strong leader as a crew chief is important.” The changes ripple through the organization. Spire offered a team-wide engineering role to Travis Peterson, who had been Michael McDowell’s crew chief. Meanwhile, Austin Dillon will also have a new crew chief in 2027. Richard Childress Racing now has Richard Boswell as vice president of competition; he served Dillon for the last two seasons. These shifts happen fast, and the drivers are left to adapt or accept the outcome. Van Gisbergen summed up the situation with a simple statement about where the power lies. “It’s up to the team, I guess,” Van Gisbergen said. The lack of driver input is now a settled fact for the 2027 season.

SCORE’s official four-wheel results, posted Sunday, put Bryce Menzies first at 16:28:29.367 and Alan Ampudia second at 16:30:07.814, a gap of 1:38.447 the other way. Ampudia crossed the line first, and he also had the lower elapsed time. What flipped the order was a set of time credits and speed penalties, and the biggest piece of it is a credit that the published report lists by amount, not by cause. That’s the detail worth sitting with. The result changing isn’t news; it’s how this race has always been scored. Elapsed time was a seesaw all day. Menzies led at mile 340 , Ampudia took more than six minutes out of him in sector 8 alone, and Menzies won back nearly five minutes over the last two sectors. They are acknowledged during team meetings while Smart tries to preach patience and reassure them opportunities are coming. “Every day, we start a team meeting with some kind of development feature of a scout team highlight, this kid’s over here working his tail off, busting his ass, look how much better he’s getting,” Smart said. “It gives some self worth to those guys, who might typically just jump in the portal. We’re trying to say, you’re going to be the guy in the coming years. Just keep doing what you’re doing.”

item.description: On this day 26 years ago, Frank Thomas has his third MVP “stolen” from him. | (Photo by DAVID MAXWELL/AFP via Getty Images) 1945 Harry Grabiner , the longest-tenured executive in White Sox history and certainly one of the longest-running employees overall, resigned as GM of the club. While not really formally holding a GM title, Grabiner had run the White Sox in tandem with three generations of Comiskey ownership, dating back to 1915. He first caught on with the team in 1905, selling scorecards; the 15-year-old got the job after noticing owner Charles Comiskey working the Comiskey Park infield after a rainstorm and asking if he could help out. By 1916, Grabiner was the team secretary (the de facto GM), at just 26. In 1939 upon the death of Comiskey’s son, Louis , the will stipulated that Grabiner was guaranteed another 10 years of employment in running the White Sox. However, Grabiner’s health was in decline, forcing his leave six years later. Grabiner would soon return to baseball, as part of Bill Veeck ’s ownership group in Cleveland. Meanwhile in Chicago, sabermetrics pioneer Les O’Connor took over the club for the next three seasons. Also on this day came some administrative news of a different sort. With Hall of Fame voting at this time occurring just once every three years, just one player and two people overall had been elected to the Hall of Fame over the previous five years. With a massive pileup of worthy players were clogging the ballot, Cooperstown decided to hold a runoff election in order to get more players into the Hall — but the move was ineffective, as no one reached the necessary 75% for election. That included legendary White Sox hurler Ed Walsh , who received just 137 of 247 (55.5%) of votes, finishing third overall on the ballot. 1948 After six years with the White Sox (interrupted right in the middle by three seasons lost to military service in World War II), Taffy Wright was sold to Philadelphia. Wright logged 12.5 in his White Sox career, was an average or better player in four of six seasons, and earned MVP votes in three. By 1948, with the right fielder’s WAR winnowed down to 0.5 over a full season of play, Chicago cut ties. item.title: Arsenal Can Win the Champions League, But Let’s Not Get Carried Away
item.description: Arsenal Can Win the Champions League, But Let’s Not Get Carried Away There’s a lot of talk among Arsenal fans and in the media about us winning the Champions League this season. I think we can all agree that we’d love to see Mikel Arteta’s side go one better than last season, when we finished runners-up to French giants PSG. But honestly, how realistic is that? It’s not impossible, of course, and we’re admittedly one of the competition’s favourites. Getting our hands on the trophy is obviously the aim. But I can’t say I feel overconfident this season, and I don’t think we should get too carried away in any competition. Fleetwood Was a Warning for Arsenal Anything can happen in football, as we certainly know after bowing out of the League Cup on penalties to League Two Fleetwood Town. They hadn’t even practised penalties before the game , and it was one of our worst displays in our entire history. If we get carried away in the Champions League, as perhaps we did in the League Cup, we could slip up once we get past the league phase, which we’ve started well. I’m not saying we should go in feeling like underdogs. But if we came up against PSG in the final again, or even Bayern Munich, who we arguably struggled against already this season, we could find ourselves on the losing end again. We haven’t established ourselves as one of the outright giants of the Champions League. We haven’t won European silverware in over 30 years, which the likes of Bayern, PSG, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Chelsea can’t relate to. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) PSG Showed How Far Arsenal Still Have to Go That has to be kept in perspective, but it shouldn’t dampen all our hopes either. I do think we were lucky to draw Atlético Madrid in the semis last season, having already beaten them in the competition. It was a tighter contest that time, but I don’t think we’d have reached the final if we’d come up against PSG instead. I can see them making this season’s final for a third time in a row. We struggled against PSG in the 2025 semi-final, and although we looked stronger against them in last season’s final , they still had us chasing shadows at times. They could’ve thrashed us in extra time, but we held out. We peaked too early when Kai Havertz gave us the lead inside the opening ten minutes, and it was 1-1 after extra time before we lost on penalties. For me, we didn’t really look like European winners that night. Even this season, we only just beat Slavia Prague 2-1, a side we should’ve scored three or four against on paper, if not more. It would be great to win the Champions League and retain the Premier League title this season. But let’s not get carried away! COYG!! item.title: How to have a scoreless draw in baseball
item.description: There’s a lot of old timey baseball things that don’t exist in the modern MLB. One notable one is ties. Now, it’s not that they didn’t play extra innings back in the early decades, they did. The issue was that for a long time stadiums did not have lights. Eventually, things got to a point where you literally could not play anymore. Leagues like NPB in Japan still have ties, but MLB has specifically created rules (the extra innings automatic runner) to ensure that games don’t go too long and end with a winner. However, that wasn’t always the case. Sometimes, that could lead to some funny box scores, like this one from 1919. Very early in the 1919 season, the Yankees were hosting the Washington Senators on May 11th . The game that day was a makeup one after a scheduled meeting two days prior was postponed due to “wet grounds.” There’s another old timey baseball thing that you don’t really see today. The Yankees faced a difficult task that day as starting on the mound for Washington was future Hall of Famer Walter Johnson. However, Yankees starter Jack Quinn was up to the challenge himself, although it would be a difficult journey. In the second inning, the Senators put their first two runners on base thanks to a single and an error, but Quinn managed to work around that by getting two big strikeouts for the first two outs. That would become a pretty common occurrence for the Yankees on the day. In the third, Quinn allowed a single to Johnson himself, before getting out of the inning with a double play. In the fourth, Quinn got an out on a fielder’s choice play at home and then had to strand the bases loaded, but managed to do so. Meanwhile, the Yankees’ offense wasn’t exactly holding up their end of the bargain against Johnson. Roger Peckinpaugh had actually singled in their second at-bat of the day, but he ended up stranded at second. After that, Johnson retired the next 28 batters. If you did the math correctly, you may have realized that’s more consecutive batters retired than what a pitcher does in a regulation perfect game. item.title: 'If the president calls, I'll be back!' - Ronaldinho teases Ravenna return
item.description: Ravenna v Forli: Serie C - Getty Images Sport Brazilian icon Ronaldinho has admitted that his sensational return to professional football at the age of 46 'went by too fast' following his debut for Ravenna. The former Ballon d'Or winner stepped back onto the pitch for the Serie C side on Sunday, proving that his love for the game remains undimmed despite years away from the spotlight. A legend returns to the pitch The footballing world stood still on Sunday as one of the game's greatest entertainers made an unexpected return to the professional ranks. Ronaldinho, now 46 years old, pulled on the Ravenna shirt for their high-stakes Serie C clash against local rivals Forli, helping his side secure a 2-0 victory . Having officially retired from the professional game in 2018 - with his last top-level match coming for Fluminense back in 2015 - the Brazilian's move to Ravenna over the summer was viewed by many as a marketing masterstroke. However, he proved he still had the hunger for competition by featuring in the starting line-up. The veteran playmaker lasted the entire first half before receiving a thunderous standing ovation during the interval, marking the end of his planned contribution to the match. Reflecting on the whirlwind experience, the Brazilian was clearly moved by the reception he received from the Italian public. 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me,' the 46-year-old explained to Sky Sport Italia . His presence was not just for show; he was heavily involved in the build-up to the opening goal scored by Giulio Donati, a player who ironically faced Ronaldinho's Milan side while playing for Lecce years ago. Future appearances on the cards While many expected this to be a one-off ceremonial appearance, Ronaldinho has already opened the door to pulling on the boots again. The Brazilian legend was substituted at half-time with Ravenna leading 1-0, prompting a media frenzy as journalists gathered around him. His former Brazil and AC Milan team-mate Dida also joined him on the pitch during the interval. The sold-out fixture at the Stadio Bruno Benelli even featured a temporary stand named the 'R10', in tribute to Ronaldinho and the iconic shirt number he wore throughout his career. item.title: Michigan hockey secures back-to-back blowout wins over Penn State
item.description: Last year, the Michigan hockey team played Penn State five times — a litany of thrilling encounters, culminating in the Wolverines sending the Nittany Lions home in the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament. And it’s first two encounters this season got off to a similar explosive start, as Michigan rained goals galore in a home sweep. Game One It took the Wolverines less than two minutes to open the fireworks, as defensemen Ben Robertson and Dakoda Rheaume-Mullen set up forward Jack Nesbitt for the first goal of the game. Less than two minutes later, defenseman Drew Schock got on the board, and by just the sixth minute of the first period, forward Malcolm Spence put Michigan up 3-0 on a power play. Two minutes later, forward Justin Poirier pulled one back on a Penn State power play. In the second period, things briefly got interesting. A few minutes in, forward Shea Busch pulled another back for the Nittany Lions to get within a goal. But forward Aidan Park drove in a fourth for insurance, to put the Wolverines up 4-2 by the end of the second. About four minutes into the third, Penn State ran back the script, when forward Reese Laubach gave the Nittany Lions a third goal. But with two to go, forward Nick Moldenhauer drove in the dagger, and Robertson’s empty netted called game. Final score: Michigan 6, Penn State 3 Game Two Night two was largely much less complicated for the Wolverines — it was an outright pummeling. The first period was somewhat restrained, with a power play goal from forward Jayden Perron and another from forward J.P. Hurlbert being all that was worth writing about. In the second, though, Michigan’s advantage exploded, thanks in part to a penalty-riddled outing from the Nittany Lions. The Wolverines rained down four power play goals — two from Perron, one from forward Michael Hage, and another from Schock. Penn State chipped in in similar fashion in the dying seconds of the period, with Busch adding a power play goal of his own. Four goals followed in the third, two a piece…and you might be able to guess where they all came from. Spence and Hurlbert added two for Michigan either side of a Poirier effort for the Nittany Lions, and defenseman Mac Gadowsky added a consolation goal in the dying seconds of the third. All on the power play. Very fitting Final score: Michigan 8, Penn State 3

item.title: 49ers Face Road Grind In Dallas Showdown With Purdy
item.description: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the road for a long stretch that could define their season. Six of their final nine games will happen away from Levi’s Stadium, starting with a trip to AT&T Stadium in Dallas. The team has to win on the road to secure the top seed in the NFC and earn a bye in the playoffs. This trip is just the start of a grueling schedule that includes stops in Mexico City, New York, and Kansas City. Coach Kyle Shanahan knows the toll travel takes on a team. He noted that the routine of being away from families gets tough after a while. “Just being away for a while, I think adds up,” Shanahan said. He added that “Just guys being away from the routine of their families and things like that, so that usually gets old by the end and everyone’s screaming to get back.” The team is trying to use the travel to their advantage by acclimating to different environments before big games. Travel Schedule and Altitude Prep The 49ers have a unique plan to handle the physical demands of the season. They will spend eight nights in strange beds across three cities. The team is using a trip to Colorado to get ready for a game in Mexico City, where the altitude is 7,350 feet. Shanahan believes this preparation helps the team during the actual games. “It’s things that we feel helps us a little bit during the game which makes it worth it, but it does get old to be away for that long,” he said. This strategy worked before when the team flew to Australia for their season opener against the Rams. The time difference and travel helped them get ready for the start of the season. Now they face a similar challenge with less time to rest. The team will go to Mexico City, then back to Santa Clara, then to New York, and back home again before heading to Los Angeles and Kansas City. It is a non-stop run that requires focus.
